summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -5 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.5%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.2%. Key releases ahead: US Core PCE Price Index m/m (11-25 8:30 AM ET); US Prelim GDP q/q (11-25 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.92% (-21 bp in a month), 2-year 4.63% (-18 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-3 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 104.43 (+2.6% in a month, +6.3% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.924 (+17.3% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.655 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 19.12 (+2.1%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -4.9% in a month (+5.9% YTD); VIX 27.4. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 80.56 $/bbl (-20.2% in a month), Brent 87.20, ULSD 3.672 $/gal (-21.5%), natural gas 3.52 (+0.4%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -13.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.1%, Hang Seng -3.1%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 6 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (18%); S&P GSCI -15.0% in a month; gold -8.9%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.

events_ahead.title: Core PCE Price Index m/m
events_ahead.why: Inflation sets rates and real yields; commodities as an inflation hedge
